economic_intuition: Corporate asset expansion tends to be followed by abnormally low returns, while asset contraction tends to be followed by abnormally high returns; annual asset growth negatively predicts subsequent stock returns.
detailed_definition: Annual firm asset growth rate, defined as the year-on-year percentage change in total assets.

evidence.location: Section I Data p.1613 Equation (1); Appendix p.1648
evidence.interpretation: Data6 is Compustat total assets, so the machine formula is (at_t_minus_1 - at_t_minus_2) / at_t_minus_2.

evidence.location: Section I Data p.1613; Table II caption p.1617
evidence.quote: "we form all of our accounting variables at the end of June in year t, using accounting information from fiscal year-end t−1"; portfolios are held "from July of year t to June of year t+1"
evidence.interpretation: This supports June formation, annual rebalance, 12-month holding period, and approximately 6-month accounting lag.

evidence.location: Section I Data p.1613; Appendix p.1648
evidence.quote: "a firm must have nonzero total assets in both years t−1 and t−2"
evidence.interpretation: The paper does not state general imputation; this requirement implies dropping observations without usable nonzero assets for ASSETG.

portfolio.universe: NYSE, Amex, and NASDAQ nonfinancial firms listed on CRSP monthly stock return files and Compustat annual industrial files.

implied_factor_direction.note: Paper reports high-minus-low spread comparisons but does not explicitly define a tradable simple long-short strategy. Direction is inferred for backtesting from the negative high-minus-low spread / high ASSETG -> low returns relation.

comparison_policy.note: Paper reports high-minus-low spreads. If backtest constructs an implied low-minus-high factor, multiply by -1 before comparing to paper-reported spreads.

source.location: Section II.A Cross-Sectional Tests p.1622; Table II caption pp.1617-1621
source.quote: "we calculate monthly returns for EW and VW portfolios for the next 12 months"; "Panel B.1 reports average monthly raw returns ... Panel B.2 reports average monthly raw returns"
source.interpretation: The paper evaluates the main Year 1 raw-return spread using average monthly raw returns on EW and VW asset-growth decile portfolios held from July of year t to June of year t+1. Input-return components: ret_i,m: monthly stock return for firm i in month m; w_i,t: portfolio weight for value-weighted portfolios; asset_growth_decile: portfolio formed from June(t) ASSETG decile cutoffs

return_combination.note: This is the paper-reported spread direction. The implied backtest factor direction may be low-minus-high because high asset growth predicts lower returns.

source.location: Section II.A Cross-Sectional Tests p.1622; Table II caption pp.1617-1621
source.quote: "we calculate monthly returns for EW and VW portfolios for the next 12 months"; "Panel B.1 reports average monthly raw returns ... Panel B.2 reports average monthly raw returns"
source.interpretation: The paper evaluates the main Year 1 raw-return spread using average monthly raw returns on EW and VW asset-growth decile portfolios held from July of year t to June of year t+1.

portfolio_return.interpretation: Stocks are sorted into asset-growth deciles at the end of June. The paper reports average monthly raw returns for equal-weighted and value-weighted decile portfolios and high-minus-low spreads.

source.location: Section II.A p.1622; Table II Panel B.1 Year 1
source.interpretation: Equal-weighted high-minus-low raw monthly return spread for Year 1.

source.location: Section II.A p.1622; Table II Panel B.2 Year 1
source.interpretation: Value-weighted high-minus-low raw monthly return spread for Year 1.

extraction_sources.ref: Asset Growth and the Cross Section of Stock Returns.pdf

ambiguous_fields.reason: Paper states asset-growth decile cutoffs but does not explicitly state whether ASSETG cutoffs use NYSE-only stocks or all eligible stocks. Full-sample cutoffs are plausible because the paper says all stocks are allocated into deciles, while NYSE breakpoints are explicitly stated only for size-group controls; however, this should be confirmed by Review Gate before original-method codegen.

evidence.location: Table II caption p.1617; Section II.A p.1622
evidence.quote: "formed based on June(t) asset growth decile cutoffs"; "using the 30th and 70th NYSE market equity percentiles"
evidence.interpretation: The first quote supports decile cutoffs for ASSETG; the second quote limits explicit NYSE breakpoint language to size grouping. The exact ASSETG breakpoint universe is therefore unspecified in the paper text.
